newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai exports down slightly, imports up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai exports down slightly, imports up.

text.p: Shanghai exported $17.66 billion worth of goods in the first nine months of 1996, down by 0.1 percent from the same 1995 period, the Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.
Shanghai's import rose by a year-on-year 15.9 percent to $17.17 billion, Xinhua said, quoting customs officials.
Foreign-funded enterprises accounted for 48.3 percent of the city's total foreign trade between January and September, compared with 37.4 percent in the year-ago period, the agency said.
Exports and imports of state enterprises continued to shrink, totalling $17.46 billion in the first nine months, or down by a year-on-year 12.3 percent, Xinhua said. It gave no further details.
